Review: bind publication to the verified candidate

review

This change removes a rebuild between validation and upload. Review the ownership boundary first, then the focused behavior and proof.

What changes for the operator

The release command still builds, validates, and uploads. Internally, those stages now share one immutable candidate instead of reconstructing it between gates.

Review focus. Confirm that no path can call publication without the verification receipt for the same candidate.

Read these files in this order

  • src/release/types.ts
    Contract. Defines candidate identity and the verified receipt.
  • src/release/run.ts
    Orchestration. Threads the candidate through each stage.
  • src/release/publish.ts
    Boundary. Accepts only a verified receipt.

The meaningful change

src/release/run.ts
28-await publish(await build(config));
28+const receipt = await verify(candidate);
29+await publish(receipt);

The type carries the proof. Publication no longer has access to build configuration, so it cannot silently create a different artifact.

Review findings

  1. Medium

    The retry path must preserve the receipt

    Evidence. Network retries re-enter the publisher after the candidate is uploaded.

    Consequence. Rebuilding on retry would reopen the identity gap.

    Action. Persist and reuse the original upload receipt.

  2. Low

    The failure message can name the candidate

    Evidence. Current output reports only the stage name.

    Action. Add the candidate identifier to the terminal receipt.

Validation evidence

CheckResultWhat it establishes
Candidate contract testsPassIdentity survives each stage
Publisher retry fixturePassRetry reuses the receipt
Production uploadNot runExternal behavior remains unverified

Reviewer decision

Approve after the retry path persists the original receipt. The main ownership change is sound; that focused correction prevents the only observed route back to an unproven candidate.

Illustrative reference: replace all sample claims, dates, metrics, paths, and decisions with grounded source material.
